title: Unitary evolution of an evaporating black hole in canonical quantum gravity
authors: Sijia Wang, Robert B. Mann, Dong-han Yeom
abstract: We propose a framework for understanding the information loss paradox in the context of canonical quantum gravity. We first revisit several approaches to black hole evaporation that do not involve an event horizon. In these models, we assume that each time slice corresponds to a coherent state in the gravitational phase space. Due to this property, the quantum state associated with a given spatial configuration will have a nonzero overlap with another spatial configuration. We show how this property can account for both semi-classical dynamics and unitary time evolution. We introduce an explicit toy model that follows semi-classical time evolution at the coarse-grained level; in addition, its time evolution is unitary at the fine-grained level. The only price that one must pay is the violation of the entropy bound; we discuss reasons why this may be justifiable.
summary: This paper tackles the black hole information loss paradox by proposing a quantum gravity framework that avoids the event horizon. It demonstrates how using coherent states allows the system to maintain unitary evolution at the fundamental quantum level while reproducing semi-classical dynamics at a coarse-grained level. The work suggests that resolving the paradox may require accepting a temporary violation of the standard entropy bound.
main_problem: The paper addresses the black hole information loss paradox, reconciling general relativity's prediction of evaporation with quantum mechanics' requirement for information conservation.
main_result: The authors propose a framework using coherent states in event-horizon-free scenarios that allows for both semi-classical dynamics and fully unitary time evolution, potentially resolving the paradox.
method: The analysis employs canonical quantum gravity techniques, utilizing the Wheeler-DeWitt equation, Euclidean path integrals, and functional Schrödinger equations.
model_or_system: The system is an evaporating black hole, analyzed in approaches that avoid the classical event horizon. The formalism treats time evolution via coherent states in the gravitational phase space.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy, Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and the violation of the entropy bound.
important_parameters: The coarse-grained vs. fine-grained description, and the non-orthogonality of quasi-classical states ($\epsilon^{|	ilde{n}-	ilde{m}|}$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the existence of coherent states in the gravitational phase space and that the violation of the entropy bound may be a justifiable price for unitarity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate proposed black hole evaporation scenarios without horizons, the causal structure connecting initial and final states via Euclidean propagators, and the setup for toy models demonstrating energy conservation.
paper_structure: The paper moves from revisiting non-horizon evaporation models to introducing a coherent state framework. It then develops the formalism using path integrals and functional Schrödinger equations to show how unitarity and semi-classical limits can coexist, concluding with a discussion on the implications for entropy bounds.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the core concepts of unitary evolution, information preservation, and the necessity of non-trivial quantum corrections to classical dynamics are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
